title: Instrument Panel Center Finish Panel Removal and Installation
introduction:
The center finish panel is the broad dashboard trim surrounding the center vents and extending across above the glovebox. Its removal starts with the smaller trim panel at the right-hand end of the dashboard.

I use the magenta attachment marks as a map of where the panel is holding on. That turns a tempting dashboard tug-of-war into a controlled clip-release job. The illustration also shows the optional information center module (ICM); its electrical connection needs attention before the panel comes away.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect yourself while handling trim
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling components with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to observe these precautions may cause serious personal injury. Review the applicable precautions in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before starting.

edits.text: Use the Interior Trim Remover to release the clips securing the RH instrument panel trim panel, then remove the panel.
edits.why: RH means right-hand. The highlighted piece is the narrow vertical trim beside the outer edge of the glovebox. Work at the magenta attachment positions shown in the drawing so the tool acts near the clips rather than bending the panel across its length.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustration shows the instrument panel center finish panel with the optional ICM.
edits.why: ICM means information center module. Use the illustrated panel shape and attachment positions to orient yourself, while allowing for the equipment actually fitted to the car.

edits.text: Release the clips securing the instrument panel center finish panel and remove the panel, disconnecting the electrical connection described below if fitted.
edits.why: The highlighted panel spans the center vents and the area above the glovebox. The magenta marks identify its attachment positions. As the clips release, keep the panel supported so an optional module connection does not become the panel's last, unwilling mounting strap.

edits.text: If equipped, disconnect the ICM electrical connector before taking the panel clear of the dashboard. Use the Interior Trim Remover for the panel clip-release work.
edits.why: The inset locates the connector on the back of the module between the center vents. Separating that connection allows the panel to come away without pulling on its wiring.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connector if equipped, refit the instrument panel center finish panel and engage its clips, then refit the right-hand trim panel and engage its clips.
edits.why: The smaller end panel goes back after the broad finish panel. Reconnecting the optional module before seating the finish panel keeps its connection accessible, and engaged clips restore the panels' attachment.

editorialRevision.scope: Preparation-only known-state parked setup; all primary actions, context, introduction and finish details unchanged. Pending independent bounded review.
